title: Behavioural Interview Question Bank
content:
# Behavioural Interview Question Bank

Use STAR: Situation, Task, Action, Result. Keep answers under two minutes. Prepare stories for teamwork, conflict, failure, leadership, and a tight deadline.

title: Behavioural Interview Question Bank
content:
Example: a group project where a teammate missed a deadline. Situation and task first, then what YOU did (re-planned tasks, spoke privately, documented work), then the result (submitted on time, grade, what you would do next time).

Common prompts: "Tell me about a time you failed." "Describe a conflict in a team." "When did you learn a tool quickly?" Practise out loud. Do not memorise a script word for word.

title: Careers in Data Science
content:
# Careers in Data Science

Analyst, data scientist, and machine learning engineer are different jobs. Analysts clean data and explain trends. Data scientists prototype models and experiments. ML engineers put models into production with monitoring.

For a computer science graduate in Nairobi, a realistic first role is data analyst or junior ML engineer if you have Python, SQL, and one portfolio project.

title: Careers in Data Science
content:
A master's is not required for many analyst roles. It helps for research-heavy ML. Salaries vary widely; treat unofficial figures as unverified until you check a primary source.

Build a small end-to-end project: dataset, notebook, simple model, short write-up of limitations.

title: Cover Letter Writing Guide
content:
# Cover Letter Writing Guide

A cover letter should be under 300 words. Paragraph 1: the role and why this organisation. Paragraph 2: one project that maps to their needs. Paragraph 3: availability and a clear ask for an interview.

Do not repeat the CV. Translate coursework into their problem. For a data internship, a class dashboard becomes "I cleaned 2,000 rows and presented trends to a supervisor."

title: Cover Letter Writing Guide
content: Address a named hiring manager when you can. Close with thanks and your phone number. For Kenyan graduate schemes, mention when you can start and that you can work on-site if required.

title: Building a Portfolio Website
content:
# Building a Portfolio Website

Recruiters spend under two minutes on a student site. Show two or three projects, not ten. Each project needs a problem, what you built, the stack, and a link to code or a demo.

Use a simple layout: name, course (for example BSc Computer Science, Strathmore), one-line goal, then projects. Host on GitHub Pages.

title: Building a Portfolio Website
content: Do not hide the GitHub link. Include one project that matches the jobs you want (API, data analysis, or a small ML demo). Write in plain English, not buzzwords.

title: Software Engineer CV Template
content:
# Software Engineer CV Template

A strong internship or graduate CV for computer science students is one page. Lead with education (course, expected graduation, relevant modules), then 2–3 projects with impact, then skills, then experience.

Write bullets as action + tool + result. Example: "Built a REST API in Python and FastAPI that cut manual report time from 3 hours to 15 minutes." Avoid listing duties only.

title: Software Engineer CV Template
content:
Match the job description: if the posting asks for Git, SQL, and teamwork, those words should appear honestly in your projects. Recruiters in Nairobi and remote teams scan for that overlap in seconds.

Include a GitHub or portfolio link. Do not attach a photo. Keep margins readable and use a single font.

title: Technical Interview Practice: Algorithms
content:
# Technical Interview Practice: Algorithms

Coding screens usually mix arrays, hash maps, strings, and simple graphs. Talk while you think: restate the problem, give an example, state time complexity, then code.

Start with a brute-force idea, then improve. For internships, correct and clear code beats a clever one-liner you cannot explain.

title: Technical Interview Practice: Algorithms
content: Practise: two-sum, reverse a linked list, BFS on a grid, and SQL group-by. After each problem, write the Big-O. If you stall, say what you would test next rather than going silent.

title: Poultry Farm Manager — getting started (illustrative)
content:
How to get into Poultry Farm Manager (Agriculture and Environment): attachment, internship, graduate programme and job routes. Illustrative synthetic guidance; verify current local requirements before relying on it.
Stage 1 - Attachment during study: Attachment student (poultry production) (industrial attachment). During the course, often in a long vacation or attachment term. First exposure to poultry production; a logbook or short report of the tasks observed and done.
Stage 2 - Internship: Poultry Farm Manager intern (internship). Final year or the first months after graduating. One or two pieces of supervised work that can be described on a CV with clear results.
Stage 3 - Graduate entry: Graduate trainee (poultry production) (graduate programme). After graduating, typically a structured one to two year programme. Rotations across teams and a mentor; evidence of learning quickly and working with others.
Stage 4 - Early career: Junior Poultry Farm Manager (full-time job). First full-time role, with or without a graduate programme first. Independent delivery of routine poultry production work.
Stage 5 - Established and senior practice: Senior Poultry Farm Manager (full-time job). After several years of practice. A track record and a chosen direction, for example: senior technical officer; farm or enterprise manager; consultant; researcher; agripreneur.
Typical opportunities in Kenya (patterns, not live vacancies):

title: Poultry Farm Manager — getting started (illustrative)
content:
Industrial attachment: Continuing student whose course requires attachment. Usually 8 to 12 weeks. Apply two to three months before the attachment term or long vacation. Applicants usually show: Interest in poultry production, a basic grounding in flock management, and willingness to learn. Documents: Introduction letter from the institution; CV; insurance cover where requested; attachment logbook.
Internship: Final-year student or recent graduate. Usually 3 to 6 months. Openings appear through the year, with more around graduation periods. Applicants usually show: Coursework or a small project using flock management and biosecurity. Documents: CV; cover letter; academic transcript; certificates.
Graduate programme: Recent graduate, often within two years of finishing. Usually 12 to 24 months with rotations. Many programmes recruit once a year; check each employer's own calendar. Applicants usually show: A solid academic record, evidence of flock management and biosecurity, and teamwork. Documents: CV; academic transcript; cover letter or application questions; online assessments where used.
Full-time job: Graduate or qualified candidate ready for an entry-level role. Permanent or fixed-term contract. Openings appear through the year. Applicants usually show: Demonstrated flock management, biosecurity, feed planning through projects, attachment or earlier work. Documents: CV; cover letter; certificates; referees.

Industrial attachment: Continuing student whose course requires attachment. Usually 8 to 12 weeks. Apply two to three months before the attachment term or long vacation. Applicants usually show: Interest in law enforcement, a basic grounding in law enforcement procedures, and willingness to learn. Documents: Introduction letter from the institution; CV; insurance cover where requested; attachment logbook.
Internship: Final-year student or recent graduate. Usually 3 to 6 months. Openings appear through the year, with more around graduation periods. Applicants usually show: Coursework or a small project using law enforcement procedures and investigation basics. Documents: CV; cover letter; academic transcript; certificates.
Graduate programme: Recent graduate, often within two years of finishing. Usually 12 to 24 months with rotations. Many programmes recruit once a year; check each employer's own calendar. Applicants usually show: A solid academic record, evidence of law enforcement procedures and investigation basics, and teamwork. Documents: CV; academic transcript; cover letter or application questions; online assessments where used.

title: Police Officer — getting started (illustrative)
content:
Full-time job: Graduate or qualified candidate ready for an entry-level role. Permanent or fixed-term contract. Openings appear through the year. Applicants usually show: Demonstrated law enforcement procedures, investigation basics, community policing through projects, attachment or earlier work. Documents: CV; cover letter; certificates; referees.
Where openings are usually advertised: Public Service Commission advertisements; county public service board advertisements; international organisation careers portals.
International roles: check visa and work-permit rules and whether your qualification is recognised.

title: Public Auditor — getting started (illustrative)
content:
How to get into Public Auditor (Public Service and Development): attachment, internship, graduate programme and job routes. Illustrative synthetic guidance; verify current local requirements before relying on it.
Stage 1 - Attachment during study: Attachment student (public sector audit) (industrial attachment). During the course, often in a long vacation or attachment term. First exposure to public sector audit; a logbook or short report of the tasks observed and done.
Stage 2 - Internship: Public Auditor intern (internship). Final year or the first months after graduating. One or two pieces of supervised work that can be described on a CV with clear results.
Stage 3 - Graduate entry: Graduate trainee (public sector audit) (graduate programme). After graduating, typically a structured one to two year programme. Rotations across teams and a mentor; evidence of learning quickly and working with others.
Stage 4 - Early career: Junior Public Auditor (full-time job). First full-time role, with or without a graduate programme first. Independent delivery of routine public sector audit work.
Stage 5 - Established and senior practice: Senior Public Auditor (full-time job). After several years of practice. A track record and a chosen direction, for example: senior officer; director; policy adviser; international organisation roles; elected or appointed leadership.
Typical opportunities in Kenya (patterns, not live vacancies):

title: Public Auditor — getting started (illustrative)
content:
Industrial attachment: Continuing student whose course requires attachment. Usually 8 to 12 weeks. Apply two to three months before the attachment term or long vacation. Applicants usually show: Interest in public sector audit, a basic grounding in public sector auditing, and willingness to learn. Documents: Introduction letter from the institution; CV; insurance cover where requested; attachment logbook.
Internship: Final-year student or recent graduate. Usually 3 to 6 months. Openings appear through the year, with more around graduation periods. Applicants usually show: Coursework or a small project using public sector auditing and financial regulations. Documents: CV; cover letter; academic transcript; certificates.
Graduate programme: Recent graduate, often within two years of finishing. Usually 12 to 24 months with rotations. Many programmes recruit once a year; check each employer's own calendar. Applicants usually show: A solid academic record, evidence of public sector auditing and financial regulations, and teamwork. Documents: CV; academic transcript; cover letter or application questions; online assessments where used.
Full-time job: Graduate or qualified candidate ready for an entry-level role. Permanent or fixed-term contract. Openings appear through the year. Applicants usually show: Demonstrated public sector auditing, financial regulations, evidence gathering through projects, attachment or earlier work. Documents: CV; cover letter; certificates; referees.

Career: Records and Archives Officer (Public Service and Development). Illustrative synthetic guidance; verify current local requirements before relying on it.
Overview: Records and Archives Officer is a role in public service and development, focused on public records. Day-to-day work typically draws on records classification, archiving and digitisation. This draft description is illustrative; confirm current duties and entry requirements with employers and the relevant professional bodies.
Focus area: public records.
Core skills: records classification, archiving, digitisation, access procedures.
Helpful skills: policy literacy, report writing, stakeholder engagement, communication, teamwork, problem solving, digital literacy, time management.
Typical study areas: Public Administration; Economics; Political Science; Development Studies; International Relations; Statistics.
Typical qualification levels: Diploma; Bachelor's degree; Master's degree for senior policy roles.
Certifications to explore: Public financial management course; policy analysis training; monitoring and evaluation course; languages.
Regulation: No single licence is assumed for this role. Confirm what each employer or institution currently asks for.
Markets: Kenya; International.

title: Records and Archives Officer — getting started (illustrative)
content:
How to get into Records and Archives Officer (Public Service and Development): attachment, internship, graduate programme and job routes. Illustrative synthetic guidance; verify current local requirements before relying on it.
Stage 1 - Attachment during study: Attachment student (public records) (industrial attachment). During the course, often in a long vacation or attachment term. First exposure to public records; a logbook or short report of the tasks observed and done.
Stage 2 - Internship: Records and Archives Officer intern (internship). Final year or the first months after graduating. One or two pieces of supervised work that can be described on a CV with clear results.
Stage 3 - Graduate entry: Graduate trainee (public records) (graduate programme). After graduating, typically a structured one to two year programme. Rotations across teams and a mentor; evidence of learning quickly and working with others.
Stage 4 - Early career: Junior Records and Archives Officer (full-time job). First full-time role, with or without a graduate programme first. Independent delivery of routine public records work.
Stage 5 - Established and senior practice: Senior Records and Archives Officer (full-time job). After several years of practice. A track record and a chosen direction, for example: senior officer; director; policy adviser; international organisation roles; elected or appointed leadership.
Typical opportunities in Kenya (patterns, not live vacancies):

title: Records and Archives Officer — getting started (illustrative)
content:
Industrial attachment: Continuing student whose course requires attachment. Usually 8 to 12 weeks. Apply two to three months before the attachment term or long vacation. Applicants usually show: Interest in public records, a basic grounding in records classification, and willingness to learn. Documents: Introduction letter from the institution; CV; insurance cover where requested; attachment logbook.
Internship: Final-year student or recent graduate. Usually 3 to 6 months. Openings appear through the year, with more around graduation periods. Applicants usually show: Coursework or a small project using records classification and archiving. Documents: CV; cover letter; academic transcript; certificates.
Graduate programme: Recent graduate, often within two years of finishing. Usually 12 to 24 months with rotations. Many programmes recruit once a year; check each employer's own calendar. Applicants usually show: A solid academic record, evidence of records classification and archiving, and teamwork. Documents: CV; academic transcript; cover letter or application questions; online assessments where used.
Full-time job: Graduate or qualified candidate ready for an entry-level role. Permanent or fixed-term contract. Openings appear through the year. Applicants usually show: Demonstrated records classification, archiving, digitisation through projects, attachment or earlier work. Documents: CV; cover letter; certificates; referees.

content:
CV and interview preparation for Records and Archives Officer (Public Service and Development). Illustrative synthetic guidance; verify current local requirements before relying on it.

Skills to highlight on the CV: records classification, archiving, digitisation, access procedures, policy literacy, report writing, stakeholder engagement.
CV bullet examples to adapt: Prepared [report, analysis or document] on [subject] used by [who] to [decision or result]. Handled [task or volume] during [attachment or role] in public records, meeting [deadline or standard]. Organised or led [club, event or team] of [size], achieving [result].

- A member of the public has been sent from office to office and arrives at your desk angry. What do you do?

Stage 2 - Internship: Electric Vehicle and Battery Technician intern (internship). Final year or the first months after graduating. One or two pieces of supervised work that can be described on a CV with clear results.

title: Electric Vehicle and Battery Technician — getting started (illustrative)
content:
Typical opportunities in Kenya (patterns, not live vacancies):
Industrial attachment: Continuing student whose course requires attachment. Usually 8 to 12 weeks. Apply two to three months before the attachment term or long vacation. Applicants usually show: Interest in electric mobility, a basic grounding in battery systems, and willingness to learn. Documents: Introduction letter from the institution; CV; insurance cover where requested; attachment logbook.
Internship: Final-year student or recent graduate. Usually 3 to 6 months. Openings appear through the year, with more around graduation periods. Applicants usually show: Coursework or a small project using battery systems and high-voltage safety. Documents: CV; cover letter; academic transcript; certificates.
Graduate programme: Recent graduate, often within two years of finishing. Usually 12 to 24 months with rotations. Many programmes recruit once a year; check each employer's own calendar. Applicants usually show: A solid academic record, evidence of battery systems and high-voltage safety, and teamwork. Documents: CV; academic transcript; cover letter or application questions; online assessments where used.
